hello.note: The polite hello; the first в is silent. Привет (pree-VYET) is hi, for friends

good-night.note: At bedtime. Good evening is Добрый вечер (DOB-rihy VYE-chir)

please.note: Also you're welcome, and here you are when handing something over

thank-you.note: Большое спасибо (bal-SHO-ye spa-SEE-ba) is thank you very much

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention. To get past someone, say Разрешите (raz-ree-SHIH-tye)

speak-english.note: Вы (vih) is the polite you, safe with anyone you don't know; ты (tih) is for friends

thousand.note: Prices are in rubles: сто рублей (sto roo-BLYEY) is 100 rubles

hundred-thousand.note: Written 100 000, with spaces between the thousands

how-much.note: Point and say Сколько это стоит? (SKOL-ka E-ta STO-it), how much does this cost?

would-like.note: The polite way to order. A man says хотел, a woman хотела. The audio uses кофе (KO-fye), coffee, as the example

i-want.note: Direct, and fine in shops. The audio uses вот это (vot E-ta), this one, as the example

do-you-have.note: Literally is there ... at yours? У вас есть вода? = do you have water?

discount.note: Literally may I have a discount? Haggling is normal at markets, not in shops

card.note: Можно (may I) starts many polite requests. Cards issued outside Russia often don't work there, so carry cash

reservation.note: Бронь is short for бронирование, a booking

checkout-time.note: Во сколько? means at what time? for anything

toilet.note: Где ...? means where is ...? for anything. On the doors, М is men and Ж women

taxi.note: Most people book rides with the Yandex Go app

train-station.note: The railway station. Moscow has nine, named after where their trains go

which-train.note: В means to. The audio uses Санкт-Петербург, St Petersburg, as the example

two-tickets.note: До means as far as, and the city's ending changes after it: до Санкт-Петербурга. The audio uses St Petersburg

trip-length.note: The audio uses St Petersburg as the example

allergic.note: Add the food: ... на орехи (na a-RYE-khee) = to nuts

love-dish.note: Literally this dish pleases me a lot

table-for-two.note: На троих (na tra-IKH) for three, на четверых (na chit-vee-RIHKH) for four

tea.note: Usually black, with sugar, lemon or jam

water.note: Without gas is без газа (biz GA-za), sparkling с газом (z GA-zam)

cheers.note: To health. A short toast before drinking is the custom
